name: Driving on Registers, Reasoning on Risk
title: Driving on Registers, Reasoning on Risk: Risk-Aware Occupancy for Register-Based End-to-End Autonomous Driving
summary: RRDrive adds dense, time-aligned risk occupancy to guide multimodal trajectory generation and rank candidates using trajectory-conditioned risk queries. The paper also introduces RiskOcc4D-NAVSIM and a sensor-based risk-occupancy predictor, reporting stronger NAVSIM scores and candidate quality, especially in challenging scenes.

name: AD-Diff Bench
title: Understanding Autonomous Driving Datasets by Describing Differences between Image Subsets in Natural Language
summary: The paper studies set-difference captioning for driving datasets: compare object-centered image subsets and generate a natural-language account of their differences. It introduces AD-Diff Bench to test whether open-weight models can detect sparse, real-world dataset shifts in a reproducible way.

name: CrashDiffuser
title: CrashDiffuser: VLM-Guided Collision Intent Reasoning for Fine-Grained Safety-Critical Traffic Scenario Generation
summary: CrashDiffuser generates safety-critical traffic scenarios with control over the collision location on a target vehicle. A vision-language model selects collision intent and a diffusion planner repeatedly adapts adversarial trajectories, enabling closed-loop generation of head, rear, or side impacts.

name: PriorEye
title: PriorEye: Geospatial Visual Priors for End-to-End Autonomous Driving
summary: PriorEye augments end-to-end driving with geospatial street-view images retrieved along the planned route, giving the policy visual context beyond its live sensor range. Its dual-memory design adapts how retrieved priors are used and provides a fallback, improving NAVSIM-v2 results and resilience to sensor corruption.

name: World Engine
title: World Engine: Towards the Era of Post-Training for Autonomous Driving
summary: World Engine reconstructs interactive scenes from driving logs and generates realistic safety-critical variations of rare events. It uses these scenarios to post-train pretrained driving policies with reinforcement learning, reducing failures on long-tail situations without risky real-world exploration.

name: Gigapixel
title: Scaling Self-Play for End-to-End Driving
summary: Gigapixel is a high-throughput simulator designed for pixel-based self-play training of end-to-end driving policies. It uses lightweight perspective-rendered scenes rather than full photorealism, allowing large-scale closed-loop interaction while retaining the visual structure needed for policy learning.

name: COMPACT-VA
title: Planning-aligned Token Compression for Long-Context Autonomous Driving
summary: COMPACT-VA compresses long driving histories into a bounded working memory with a conditional VQ-VAE. Because compression is conditioned on learned planning intent, it aims to retain decision-relevant context for monolithic vision-action policies while reducing the token and inference cost of long sequences.

name: TOAD
title: Test-Time Trajectory Optimization for Autonomous Driving
summary: TOAD improves an existing trajectory planner at test time by treating its scorer as a reward and using cross-entropy search to optimize candidate trajectories. It starts from the planner's proposals, requires no retraining, and is evaluated on NAVSIM-v1/v2 and closed-loop HUGSIM.

name: NTR
title: NTR: Neural Token Reconstruction for Scene Token Bottleneck in End-to-End Driving
summary: Neural Token Reconstruction adds masked latent self-distillation to perception-free driving models so compact scene tokens must preserve information from image patches. Foundation-model semantic priors guide reconstruction toward driving-relevant content without adding explicit perception heads.

name: CLOVER
title: CLOVER: Closed-Loop Value Estimation and Ranking for End-to-End Autonomous Driving Planning
summary: CLOVER addresses the mismatch between imitation of logged paths and rule-based planning evaluation. It combines a diverse trajectory generator with a metric-aware scorer, trains on evaluator-filtered pseudo-experts, and uses conservative closed-loop self-distillation to improve proposal coverage and ranking.

name: 123D
title: 123D: Unifying Multi-Modal Autonomous Driving Data at Scale
summary: 123D provides a common API for working with autonomous-driving datasets that differ in sensors, formats, annotation conventions, and sampling rates. Its timestamped event-stream representation supports synchronous or asynchronous multimodal access, helping researchers combine datasets for training and evaluation.

name: ReflectDrive-2
title: ReflectDrive-2: Reinforcement-Learning-Aligned Self-Editing for Discrete Diffusion Driving
summary: ReflectDrive-2 represents plans as discrete trajectory tokens and lets the same model revise selected tokens through an AutoEdit step. After supervised recovery from perturbed expert plans, rollout-level reinforcement learning trains the full draft-and-reflect process, improving the value of test-time editing.

name: RAD-2
title: RAD-2: Scaling Reinforcement Learning in a Generator-Discriminator Framework
summary: RAD-2 pairs a diffusion trajectory generator with an RL-trained discriminator that reranks candidates by long-term driving quality. Temporally consistent group-relative updates and on-policy generator optimization provide structured feedback while avoiding direct optimization of sparse rewards over full trajectories.

name: MOSAIC
title: Scaling-Aware Data Selection for End-to-End Autonomous Driving Systems
summary: MOSAIC selects training data by fitting metric-specific scaling laws across dataset domains and iteratively choosing mixtures expected to improve evaluation performance. In autonomous-driving experiments, it achieves stronger EPDMS results than baselines while using substantially less training data.

name: FlowAD
title: FlowAD: Ego-Scene Interactive Modeling for Autonomous Driving
summary: FlowAD models how ego motion changes the observed scene by representing ego-scene interaction as scene flow. Its framework derives flow units from logged data, aiming to improve environment representations for driving tasks without depending on scenario simulation.

name: SparseDriveV2
title: SparseDriveV2: Scoring is All You Need for End-to-End Autonomous Driving
summary: SparseDriveV2 studies how trajectory-anchor density affects score-based end-to-end planning. Its experiments show that scaling a static trajectory vocabulary can substantially improve planning, questioning whether dynamically generated proposals are always necessary.

name: HDP
title: Unleashing the Potential of Diffusion Models for End-to-End Autonomous Driving
summary: Hyper Diffusion Planner systematically studies diffusion-based end-to-end planning choices using large-scale real-vehicle data and road tests. It combines findings on trajectory representation, diffusion training, and data scaling with reinforcement-learning post-training, and reports real-world evaluation across urban scenarios.

name: MeanFuser
title: MeanFuser: Fast One-Step Multi-Modal Trajectory Generation and Adaptive Reconstruction via MeanFlow for End-to-End Autonomous Driving
summary: MeanFuser uses Gaussian-mixture noise and MeanFlow to generate continuous multimodal trajectories without relying on a discrete anchor vocabulary. An adaptive reconstruction module can select a proposal or construct a new trajectory, while the one-step formulation targets faster planning.

name: PCM
title: A Generalizable Physics-guided Causal Model for Trajectory Prediction in Autonomous Driving
summary: PCM targets zero-shot motion-prediction generalization by separating domain-invariant scene features and combining them with vehicle kinematics. Its intervention-based scene encoder and causal ODE decoder use contextual interactions while preserving physical motion structure.

name: PlannerRFT
title: PlannerRFT: Reinforcing Diffusion Planners through Closed-Loop and Sample-Efficient Fine-Tuning
summary: PlannerRFT fine-tunes diffusion planners with a dual-branch reinforcement-learning loop: one branch improves trajectory distributions while another guides denoising toward useful exploration. Its nuMax simulator accelerates rollouts, targeting sample-efficient closed-loop adaptation without changing the planner's inference pipeline.

name: DrivoR
title: Driving on Registers
summary: DrivoR uses camera-aware register tokens to compress multi-camera features from pretrained vision transformers, then lightweight decoders generate and score trajectories. Its scorer predicts interpretable safety, comfort, and efficiency signals, with results evaluated on NAVSIM and closed-loop HUGSIM.

name: AlignDrive
title: AlignDrive: Aligned Lateral-Longitudinal Planning for End-to-End Autonomous Driving
summary: AlignDrive couples lateral path choice with speed planning: longitudinal motion is predicted along the selected path rather than independently. It also augments training with rare collision-avoidance situations, improving coordination and reported performance on Bench2Drive and Fail2Drive.

name: LEAD
title: LEAD: Minimizing Learner-Expert Asymmetry in End-to-End Driving
summary: LEAD studies why privileged simulator experts are hard for sensor-based imitation learners to copy, including visibility, uncertainty, and route-intent gaps. It proposes ways to reduce these asymmetries and reports stronger closed-loop CARLA performance plus transfer gains on NAVSIM and Waymo driving benchmarks.

name: DiffusionDriveV2
title: DiffusionDriveV2: Reinforcement Learning-Constrained Truncated Diffusion Modeling in End-to-End Autonomous Driving
summary: DiffusionDriveV2 adds reinforcement learning to an anchor-conditioned diffusion planner to suppress poor trajectory modes while preserving diverse driving intentions. Separate within-anchor and cross-anchor policy updates improve reward comparisons without collapsing distinct behaviors such as turning and going straight.

name: Spatial Retrieval AD
title: Spatial Retrieval Augmented Autonomous Driving
summary: Spatial Retrieval AD supplements live vehicle sensors with geographically retrieved street images, giving driving models prior visual context when visibility is limited. The paper builds a location-aligned nuScenes extension and evaluates the added modality across perception, mapping, occupancy, planning, and world modeling.

name: LAP
title: LAP: Fast LAtent Diffusion Planner for Autonomous Driving
summary: LAP performs diffusion planning in a learned latent space that separates high-level driving intent from low-level trajectory geometry. Feature alignment links this space to scene context, enabling one-step denoising and faster closed-loop planning on nuPlan.

name: GuideFlow
title: GuideFlow: Constraint-Guided Flow Matching for Planning in End-to-End Autonomous Driving
summary: GuideFlow uses constrained flow matching to generate diverse end-to-end driving trajectories while enforcing safety and physical constraints during generation. The method aims to avoid mode collapse and reduce the need for a separate post-generation optimization stage.

name: DiffRefiner
title: DiffRefiner: Coarse to Fine Trajectory Planning via Diffusion Refinement with Semantic Interaction for End to End Autonomous Driving
summary: DiffRefiner combines an anchor-based transformer that proposes coarse trajectories with a diffusion model that refines them. A fine-grained denoising decoder incorporates surrounding-scene semantics to produce plans that better fit the driving context.

name: MiMo-Embodied
title: MiMo-Embodied: X-Embodied Foundation Model Technical Report
summary: MiMo-Embodied is a foundation model trained across autonomous driving and broader embodied-AI tasks. The paper attributes cross-domain gains to curated data, staged training, chain-of-thought reasoning, and reinforcement-learning fine-tuning, and evaluates it on both driving and embodied benchmarks.

name: UniMM-V2X
title: UniMM-V2X: MoE-Enhanced Multi-Level Fusion for End-to-End Cooperative Autonomous Driving
summary: UniMM-V2X enables vehicles to cooperate across perception, prediction, and planning in one end-to-end multi-agent framework. Shared queries and multi-level fusion coordinate their scene understanding, while mixture-of-experts components adapt representations and motion decoding to different driving situations.

name: UniLION
title: UniLION: Towards Unified Autonomous Driving Model with Linear Group RNNs
summary: UniLION uses linear group recurrent operators to process long sequences of LiDAR, camera, and multimodal driving data with lower attention cost. A single architecture supports several sensor and temporal configurations and performs perception, prediction, and planning tasks.

name: ZTRS
title: Zero-Human Demonstration End-to-end Autonomous Driving with Trajectory Scorer
summary: ZTRS presents an end-to-end planning approach trained without human driving demonstrations, using real-world images and rule-based rewards. A trajectory scorer helps address reinforcement learning cold start and supports a fully reward-driven training pipeline.

name: EvaDrive
title: EvaDrive: Evolutionary Adversarial Policy Optimization for End-to-End Autonomous Driving
summary: EvaDrive co-evolves a trajectory generator and a multi-objective critic through adversarial reinforcement learning. Its Pareto-based selection preserves trade-offs among driving preferences instead of collapsing them into one reward, enabling repeated proposal refinement and diverse driving styles.

name: DistillDrive
title: DistillDrive: End-to-End Multi-Mode Autonomous Driving Distillation by Isomorphic Hetero-Source Planning Model
summary: DistillDrive transfers diverse planning behaviors from a structured-scene teacher into an end-to-end model using multiple planning instances, generative training examples, and reinforcement learning. On nuScenes and NAVSIM it reports fewer collisions and improved closed-loop scores.

name: DiffSemanticFusion
title: DiffSemanticFusion: Semantic Raster BEV Fusion for Autonomous Driving via Online HD Map Diffusion
summary: DiffSemanticFusion combines semantic raster BEV features with a diffusion-based online map representation to capture both visual semantics and geometric structure. It applies the fused scene representation to motion prediction and end-to-end planning, with experiments on nuScenes and NAVSIM.

name: GEMINUS
title: GEMINUS: Dual-aware Global and Scene-Adaptive Mixture-of-Experts for End-to-End Autonomous Driving
summary: GEMINUS combines a general driving expert with specialists trained for different scene types. A dual-aware router uses scene features and routing uncertainty to select experts, improving adaptive closed-loop performance in Bench2Drive, including with monocular input.

name: TrajFlow
title: TrajFlow: Multi-modal Motion Prediction via Flow Matching
summary: TrajFlow uses flow matching to predict several coherent future trajectories in one inference pass instead of repeated sampling. A Plackett-Luce ranking objective improves uncertainty estimates while keeping multimodal motion forecasting computationally efficient.

name: ETA
title: ETA: Efficiency through Thinking Ahead, A Dual Approach to Self-Driving with Large Models
summary: ETA moves expensive large-model reasoning to earlier time steps and predicts ahead asynchronously, while a smaller model handles the current frame rapidly. An action mask fuses both feature streams so large-model guidance is available with lower per-frame latency.

name: GTRS
title: Generalized Trajectory Scoring for End-to-end Multimodal Planning
summary: GTRS combines diffusion-generated fine-grained proposals with a trajectory scorer trained on a much denser vocabulary, then regularizes the scorer to work on smaller candidate sets. Sensor augmentation and refinement training target better ranking and generalization across driving domains.

name: DriveSuprim
title: DriveSuprim: Towards Precise Trajectory Selection for End-to-End Planning
summary: DriveSuprim selects safe trajectories from large candidate sets using progressive coarse-to-fine filtering. Rotation-based augmentation improves robustness to distribution shifts, while self-distillation stabilizes training; the paper evaluates it on NAVSIM and the closed-loop Bench2Drive benchmark.

name: NAVSIM
title: Pseudo-Simulation for Autonomous Driving
summary: NAVSIM proposes pseudo-simulation for evaluating driving policies from real logs: 3D Gaussian splatting generates future observations at varied positions, headings, and speeds, then behavior-proximity weights emphasize observations matching a policy's likely outcomes.

name: GaussianFusion
title: GaussianFusion: Gaussian-Based Multi-Sensor Fusion for End-to-End Autonomous Driving
summary: GaussianFusion fuses camera and other sensor features through compact, interpretable 2D Gaussian scene elements. Explicit semantic-spatial attributes and implicit planning cues are refined together, and a cascade planning head uses them to iteratively improve trajectories.

name: iPad
title: iPad: Iterative Proposal-centric End-to-End Autonomous Driving
summary: iPad makes candidate plans central to the end-to-end representation: proposal-anchored attention iteratively updates trajectories and image features. Lightweight mapping and motion-prediction tasks add planning-relevant supervision, improving benchmark performance with lower computational cost.

name: TransDiffuser
title: TransDiffuser: Diverse Trajectory Generation with Decorrelated Multi-modal Representation for End-to-end Autonomous Driving
summary: TransDiffuser aims to prevent diffusion planners from collapsing to similar trajectories without relying on predefined anchors or stored scene priors. It decorrelates multimodal latent representations during denoising so the model can produce diverse, plausible plans in NAVSIM.

name: BridgeAD
title: Bridging Past and Future: End-to-End Autonomous Driving with Historical Prediction and Planning
summary: BridgeAD assigns distinct queries to future time steps so historical scene information can support both present-frame perception and multi-step motion planning. This aligns temporal memory with the planning horizon instead of treating history as a generic feature bank.

name: Hydra-MDP++
title: Hydra-MDP++: Advancing End-to-End Driving via Expert-Guided Hydra-Distillation
summary: Hydra-MDP++ distills human and rule-based expert behavior into a lightweight raw-image driving model with a multi-head decoder. Its expanded supervision includes traffic-light compliance, lane keeping, and comfort, addressing unsafe behaviors that conventional planning scores can miss.

name: TrajHF
title: Learning Personalized Driving Styles via Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback
summary: TrajHF fine-tunes generative trajectory models with human feedback to better reflect varied driving styles. Multi-condition denoising and preference-based reinforcement learning aim to personalize multimodal plans while maintaining safety and physical feasibility.

name: HiP-AD
title: HiP-AD: Hierarchical and Multi-Granularity Planning with Deformable Attention for Autonomous Driving in a Single Decoder
summary: HiP-AD uses spatial, temporal, and driving-style waypoint queries at multiple resolutions to supervise planning. A unified decoder with deformable attention retrieves scene features around trajectory locations and jointly handles perception, prediction, and planning.

name: DriveTransformer
title: DriveTransformer: Unified Transformer for Scalable End-to-End Autonomous Driving
summary: DriveTransformer replaces a rigid perception-prediction-planning sequence with parallel interaction among agent, map, and planning queries. Sparse sensor-feature access and streaming query history aim to reduce error accumulation and support efficient long-range temporal reasoning.

name: GoalFlow
title: GoalFlow: Goal-Driven Flow Matching for Multimodal Trajectories Generation in End-to-End Autonomous Driving
summary: GoalFlow guides multimodal trajectory generation with selected goal points that constrain the flow-matching process. A scene-conditioned scoring mechanism chooses among candidate goals, targeting more coherent and higher-quality plans than unconstrained trajectory generation.

name: MomAD
title: Don't Shake the Wheel: Momentum-Aware Planning in End-to-End Autonomous Driving
summary: MomAD adds trajectory and perception momentum to stabilize end-to-end plans over time and through occlusions. It matches planning queries to prior paths and reuses historical scene features to support coherent long-horizon predictions and reduce collision risk.

name: DiffusionDrive
title: DiffusionDrive: Truncated Diffusion Model for End-to-End Autonomous Driving
summary: DiffusionDrive accelerates multimodal trajectory planning by starting from intent-specific anchors and truncating diffusion to two denoising steps. Its cascade decoder conditions trajectories on scene context, targeting real-time inference without losing candidate diversity.

name: NAVSIM
title: NAVSIM: Data-Driven Non-Reactive Autonomous Vehicle Simulation and Benchmarking
summary: NAVSIM provides a scalable, data-driven evaluation middle ground between open-loop metrics and expensive reactive simulation. It unrolls bird's-eye-view scene abstractions for short horizons and measures progress and safety in a non-reactive setting designed to align better with closed-loop outcomes.

name: Hydra-MDP
title: Hydra-MDP: End-to-end Multimodal Planning with Multi-target Hydra-Distillation
summary: Hydra-MDP distills both human and rule-based teachers into a multi-head end-to-end planner that produces diverse trajectories for different evaluation criteria. The approach learns rule-aware planning directly rather than relying on non-differentiable post-processing.

name: SparseDrive
title: SparseDrive: End-to-End Autonomous Driving via Sparse Scene Representation
summary: SparseDrive uses sparse scene representations to unify detection, tracking, and mapping, then predicts other agents and plans ego motion in parallel. The design targets safer and more efficient end-to-end driving than dense BEV pipelines.

name: VADv2
title: VADv2: End-to-End Vectorized Autonomous Driving via Probabilistic Planning
summary: VADv2 treats end-to-end planning as a probability distribution over future actions rather than deterministic regression. It tokenizes a large trajectory vocabulary and models interactions between planning tokens and scene tokens to represent uncertainty.

name: BEV-Planner
title: Is Ego Status All You Need for Open-Loop End-to-End Autonomous Driving?
summary: BEV-Planner analyzes whether open-loop end-to-end planners use visual perception or rely mainly on ego status in nuScenes. It proposes a road-adherence metric and a simple perception-light baseline to expose dataset and metric limitations.

name: VAD
title: VAD: Vectorized Scene Representation for Efficient Autonomous Driving
summary: VAD represents agents and map elements as vectors instead of dense raster grids, preserving instance-level structure for planning. These explicit scene elements act as constraints for safer trajectories while reducing the cost of BEV processing and post-processing.

name: UniAD
title: Planning-oriented Autonomous Driving
summary: UniAD organizes perception, prediction, and planning around the final driving objective rather than optimizing separate task heads in isolation. Its unified network coordinates the full driving stack so scene understanding and forecasting directly support planning.

name: ST-P3
title: ST-P3: End-to-end Vision-based Autonomous Driving via Spatial-Temporal Feature Learning
summary: ST-P3 jointly learns spatial and temporal features for vision-based perception, prediction, and planning. Egocentric feature accumulation preserves geometry, while temporal pathways model motion and refine planning features for closed-loop control.

name: TransFuser
title: TransFuser: Imitation with Transformer-Based Sensor Fusion for Autonomous Driving
summary: This TransFuser version fuses camera and LiDAR features with multi-scale transformer attention across perspective and bird's-eye views. It targets complex, dense-traffic scenarios in CARLA and reports improved driving scores and fewer collisions than geometry-based fusion.

name: NEAT
title: NEAT: Neural Attention Fields for End-to-End Autonomous Driving
summary: NEAT represents a driving scene as a neural attention field that maps bird's-eye-view locations to semantics and waypoints. Its attention-based compression lets an imitation policy focus on relevant image regions while offering interpretable visualizations.

name: Roach
title: End-to-End Urban Driving by Imitating a Reinforcement Learning Coach
summary: Roach trains a reinforcement-learning driving expert using privileged bird's-eye-view information, then uses that expert as a dense coach for an end-to-end imitation learner. The resulting camera-based policy generalizes across CARLA towns and weather.

name: IVMP
title: Learning Interpretable End-to-End Vision-Based Motion Planning for Autonomous Driving with Optical Flow Distillation
summary: IVMP predicts future semantic maps in bird's-eye view from surrounding camera images, then plans through these interpretable forecasts. Explicit future scene structure helps the planner account for less likely objects and improve safety.

name: TransFuser
title: Multi-Modal Fusion Transformer for End-to-End Autonomous Driving
summary: The original TransFuser uses transformer attention to combine camera and LiDAR features, enabling global scene reasoning beyond local geometric fusion. Its CARLA experiments show stronger behavior in complex traffic interactions and fewer collisions than prior fusion baselines.

name: MP3
title: MP3: A Unified Model to Map, Perceive, Predict and Plan
summary: MP3 enables mapless driving from raw sensors and a route command by jointly predicting an online map and agent futures, then planning with an uncertainty-aware neural motion planner. It is evaluated in long closed-loop simulations and real-world data.

name: P3
title: Perceive, Predict, and Plan: Safe Motion Planning Through Interpretable Semantic Representations
summary: P3 jointly learns perception, prediction, and planning through a semantic-occupancy representation. The planner uses costs aligned with the model's scene predictions, yielding interpretable decisions and safer trajectories in datasets and closed-loop simulation.

name: Data Aggregation
title: Exploring Data Aggregation in Policy Learning for Vision-Based Urban Autonomous Driving
summary: This study analyzes DAgger-style data aggregation for vision-based urban driving and proposes sampling behaviorally important states into a replay buffer focused on uncertain regions. On CARLA NoCrash it improves generalization in dense traffic while reducing collisions.

name: Implicit Affordances
title: End-to-End Model-Free Reinforcement Learning for Urban Driving Using Implicit Affordances
summary: Implicit Affordances uses learned latent affordance signals to make reinforcement learning practical for complex urban driving tasks such as lane keeping, obstacle avoidance, and traffic-light response. The approach demonstrates camera-only driving in the CARLA challenge.

name: iDriveVLA
title: Evaluation Is All You Need for Multi-Modal Autonomous Driving
summary: iDriveVLA improves multimodal planning by pairing a safety-aware trajectory scorer with a vision-language module that adjusts evaluation criteria to the scene. Its progressive, oracle-aligned training refines candidate generation and ranking, achieving strong results on the NAVSIM-v1 leaderboard.

name: Run-then-Walk
title: Sometimes You Gotta Run Before You Can Walk: Run-then-Walk Scheduling Strategy for VLM Autonomous Driving
summary: Run-then-Walk separates reinforcement learning for VLA driving into a progress-seeking phase followed by a safety-repair phase. This staged reward schedule aims to escape overly conservative behavior first, then correct unsafe actions, improving performance and convergence over one-stage training.

name: Qwen-Drive-1.0
title: Qwen-Drive-1.0: An Initial Step towards a Vision-Language Foundation Model for Autonomous Driving
summary: Qwen-Drive-1.0 integrates 3D perception, visual question answering, and motion planning around a pretrained vision-language model. An inspectable BEV head exposes scene structure, while a planning expert predicts trajectories; staged driving and general VLM training seeks to retain broad visual and instruction abilities.

name: HybridDriveVLA
title: HybridDriveVLA: Vision-Language-Action Model with Visual CoT reasoning and ToT Evaluation for Autonomous Driving
summary: HybridDriveVLA anticipates future scenes with visual chain-of-thought, then scores candidate waypoints for safety, progress, and comfort using a tree-of-thought evaluator.

name: Plug-and-Play
title: Plug-and-Play Traffic Element Awareness for End-to-End Autonomous Driving
summary: This study adds structured traffic-light and road-sign awareness to end-to-end driving systems through a lightweight plug-and-play interface. It also augments public datasets with traffic-element annotations and evaluates the effect across regression, diffusion, trajectory-scoring, and VLA planners.

name: BrainWAM
title: BrainWAM: Action-Space Coordination of Semantic Priors and Predictive Dynamics for Autonomous Driving
summary: BrainWAM coordinates semantic reasoning from a vision-language model with predictive dynamics from a world-action model. Instead of mixing both through shared token attention, it routes them through specialized action pathways and aligns their compact action representations.

name: DriveVLA-M0
title: DriveVLA-M0: Failure-Aware Memory Augmentation for Autonomous Driving
summary: DriveVLA-M0 stores past failures with scene structure and expert trajectories, then retrieves structurally similar cases at test time. A lightweight LoRA-based update uses the retrieved examples to correct distribution-shift errors without changing the model backbone.

name: FactorDrive
title: FactorDrive: Adaptive Multi-Step Reasoning Driven by Planning-Critical Factors for End-to-End Autonomous Driving
summary: FactorDrive grounds multi-step driving reasoning in planning-critical spatial and physical evidence. It introduces a factor-based chain-of-thought dataset and adapts reasoning depth to the scene, then studies post-training aimed at improving planning decisions.

name: DEFT-RLVR
title: Deferred Exposure of Future Trajectories for Verifiable Reasoning in Autonomous Driving VLMs
summary: DEFT-RLVR addresses bias caused when a reasoning model sees the logged future trajectory before explaining a driving decision. It frames planning as choosing among explicit candidates and uses future trajectories after the decision as verifiable targets for reinforcement learning.

name: WorkDrive
title: WorkDrive: Roadwork Chain of Causation for Autonomous Driving
summary: WorkDrive targets roadwork zones where temporary cones and barriers change the usual road layout. It builds perception-grounded causal explanations from structured scene facts, trains the model on them, and uses trajectory-consistency reinforcement learning to improve work-zone planning.

name: Post-Training Survey
title: Post-Training in End-to-End Autonomous Driving
summary: This survey organizes post-training methods for end-to-end autonomous-driving models, including both VLA systems and trajectory-generative planners. It explains why imitation alone is insufficient in interactive safety-critical driving, then compares supervision families, their trade-offs, and open problems.

name: LingBot-VLA 2.0
title: From Foundation to Application: Improving VLA Models in Practice
summary: LingBot-VLA 2.0 expands a generalist robotics VLA with larger cross-embodiment data, a broader action space, and predictive dynamics for temporal reasoning. Its evaluation spans embodied-AI benchmarks and long-horizon mobile manipulation across robot platforms.

name: AnchorVLA
title: AnchorVLA: Bridging Discrete Decisions and Continuous Trajectories for Vision-Language-Action Planning
summary: AnchorVLA connects language-level driving decisions to continuous trajectories through behavior-pattern anchors. Each anchor represents a local motion pattern, providing a denser interface between VLA reasoning and executable path generation than long sequences of coordinate tokens.

name: DriveTeach-VLA
title: Teaching Vision-Language-Action Models What to See and Where to Look
summary: DriveTeach-VLA trains driving models to attend to spatially relevant visual evidence, not only text-centric question-answering and reasoning. It combines driving-aware visual distillation with trajectory-guided prompts, followed by supervised and reinforcement fine-tuning.

name: WVM
title: World Value Models for Robotic Manipulation
summary: World Value Model applies temporally predictive world-model representations to assess the value and quality of robotic experiences. It is a cross-domain robotics method rather than a driving-specific planner, and reports improved value ordering on manipulation benchmarks.

name: DriveReward
title: DriveReward: A Comprehensive Dataset and Generative Vision-Language Reward Model for Autonomous Driving
summary: DriveReward introduces a temporally grounded dataset for evaluating driving trajectories, including counterfactual styles and failures, alongside a specialized vision-language reward model. Its compact model is tested for reward alignment, trajectory scoring, and reinforcement-learning fine-tuning.

name: ChainFlow-VLA
title: ChainFlow-VLA: Causal Flow Planning with Vision-Language Models
summary: ChainFlow-VLA combines an autoregressive model for causally ordered interaction modes with a diffusion refiner for global trajectory consistency. VLM-derived semantic features condition residual corrections while preserving the causal structure of the initial plan.

name: IKN
title: Grounding Driving VLA via Inverse Kinematics
summary: IKN reframes driving trajectory prediction as inverse kinematics and argues that current and future visual states are both needed to ground actions. It predicts the next visual scene, then uses a separate conditional diffusion network to decode trajectories from visual states.

name: CRAFT
title: CRAFT: Counterfactual-to-Interactive Reinforcement Fine-Tuning for Driving Policies
summary: CRAFT fine-tunes driving policies by combining dense counterfactual trajectory advantages with corrections from closed-loop interaction events. An EMA teacher regularizes the update, aiming to retain stable behavior while making reinforcement fine-tuning more sample-efficient.

name: OneDrive
title: OneDrive: Unified Multi-Paradigm Driving with Vision-Language-Action Models
summary: OneDrive unifies language generation, object perception, and trajectory planning in one transformer decoder built on a pretrained vision-language model. Visual context and structured query tokens share the decoder, reducing the need for separate or cascaded task-specific heads.

name: UniDriveVLA
title: UniDriveVLA: Unifying Understanding, Perception, and Action Planning for Autonomous Driving
summary: UniDriveVLA separates driving understanding, 3D scene perception, and action planning into specialized experts coordinated through masked attention. Sparse perception and staged training aim to improve spatial grounding without sacrificing the language model's reasoning ability.

name: DVGT-2
title: DVGT-2: Vision-Geometry-Action Model for Autonomous Driving at Scale
summary: DVGT-2 uses streaming dense-geometry prediction as an alternative to language-heavy driving VLA designs. Causal temporal attention and cached history jointly support online scene-geometry estimation and trajectory planning without repeatedly processing full multi-frame batches.

name: AutoDrive-P3
title: $AutoDrive\text{-}P^3$: Unified Chain of Perception-Prediction-Planning Thought via Reinforcement Fine-Tuning
summary: AutoDrive-P3 trains a VLA to reason coherently through perception, prediction, and planning rather than skipping intermediate evidence or treating tasks separately. It introduces a structured P3 chain-of-thought dataset and hierarchical reinforcement fine-tuning across the three stages.

name: Learning from Mistakes
title: Learning from Mistakes: Post-Training for Driving VLA with Takeover Data
summary: TakeVLA learns proactively from takeover failures by adding language supervision about hazards before the human intervention, expanding safety margins. The framework also uses active exploration so post-training can improve beyond passively imitating takeover trajectories.

name: AutoMoT
title: AutoMoT: A Unified Vision-Language-Action Model with Asynchronous Mixture-of-Transformers for End-to-End Autonomous Driving
summary: AutoMoT unifies scene reasoning and action generation in an asynchronous mixture-of-transformers, sharing a model while running slower reasoning and faster control at different rates.

name: DynVLA
title: DynVLA: Learning World Dynamics for Action Reasoning in Autonomous Driving
summary: DynVLA introduces Dynamics CoT: compact tokens forecast ego and environment evolution before the model chooses an action. This provides physically grounded temporal context with less redundancy than textual or dense visual chain-of-thought.

name: EvoDriveVLA
title: EvoDriveVLA: Evolving Driving VLA Models via Collaborative Perception-Planning Distillation
summary: EvoDriveVLA uses collaborative teachers to improve both visual grounding and future-aware planning. Self-anchored visual distillation stabilizes perception, while a future-informed teacher refines trajectory reasoning to reduce errors over long horizons.

name: Curious-VLA
title: Devil is in Narrow Policy: Unleashing Exploration in Driving VLA Models
summary: Curious-VLA tackles limited exploration in imitation-trained driving agents by expanding feasible trajectory options during supervised learning and prioritizing diverse experiences during reinforcement learning. A wider, style-aware reward signal helps distinguish driving quality.

name: LaST-VLA
title: LaST-VLA: Thinking in Latent Spatio-Temporal Space for Vision-Language-Action in Autonomous Driving
summary: LaST-VLA reasons in a continuous spatiotemporal latent space instead of relying on explicit text chain-of-thought. It aligns geometry from 3D foundation models with future dynamics from world models, then progressively learns trajectory generation and safety-aware refinement.

name: LinkVLA
title: Unifying Language-Action Understanding and Generation for Autonomous Driving
summary: LinkVLA aligns language and actions through a shared discrete codebook, adds trajectory-to-caption supervision, and uses coarse-to-fine decoding to cut inference time.

name: ELF-VLA
title: Unleashing VLA Potentials in Autonomous Driving via Explicit Learning from Failures
summary: ELF-VLA adds structured failure diagnosis to reinforcement learning for driving VLA models. Its interpretable reports distinguish planning, reasoning, and trajectory-execution errors, providing actionable feedback when ordinary scalar rewards plateau on long-tail scenarios.

name: NoRD
title: NoRD: A Data-Efficient Vision-Language-Action Model that Drives without Reasoning
summary: NORD reduces reliance on large driving datasets and costly reasoning annotations, achieving competitive results with a smaller training set and fewer generated tokens. The paper also identifies difficulty bias in GRPO and applies Dr. GRPO to improve reinforcement learning on challenging scenarios.

name: VGGDrive
title: VGGDrive: Empowering Vision-Language Models with Cross-View Geometric Grounding for Autonomous Driving
summary: VGGDrive equips a vision-language model with cross-view 3D geometric grounding by injecting features from a frozen 3D foundation model. Its hierarchical geometric enabler aims to preserve the base VLM while improving spatial understanding across driving evaluation protocols.

name: HiST-VLA
title: HiST-VLA: A Hierarchical Spatio-Temporal Vision-Language-Action Model for End-to-End Autonomous Driving
summary: HiST-VLA combines 3D geometric cues, fine-grained driving commands, and historical state prompts for more reliable trajectory generation. Dynamic token sparsification fuses redundant tokens to improve efficiency without simply dropping potentially useful context.

name: Dual-System Driving
title: From Representational Complementarity to Dual Systems: Synergizing VLM and Vision-Only Backbones for End-to-End Driving
summary: This study compares vision-language and vision-only driving backbones, finding that each retains distinct behaviorally useful features after policy training. It exploits their complementarity in HybridDriveVLA, running both branches and selecting trajectories with a learned scorer.

name: SparseOccVLA
title: SparseOccVLA: Bridging Occupancy and Vision-Language Models via Sparse Queries for Unified 4D Scene Understanding and Planning
summary: SparseOccVLA bridges VLM reasoning and 4D occupancy with compact sparse queries, then uses an anchor-diffusion planner for scene understanding, forecasting, and trajectory planning.

name: SGDrive
title: SGDrive: Scene-to-Goal Hierarchical World Cognition for Autonomous Driving
summary: SGDrive structures driving reasoning around a scene-agent-goal hierarchy: understand the overall context, focus on safety-critical agents, then formulate short-term goals before acting. This hierarchy is designed to make a general VLM's representations more useful for 3D driving.

name: FLARE
title: FLARE: Learning Future-Aware Latent Representations from Vision-Language Models for Autonomous Driving
summary: FLARE activates pretrained VLM visual knowledge without labor-intensive language labels by predicting future scene features and ego motion in latent space. It then uses reinforcement learning to refine trajectory decisions from unlabeled driving data.

name: ColaVLA
title: ColaVLA: Leveraging Cognitive Latent Reasoning for Hierarchical Parallel Trajectory Planning in Autonomous Driving
summary: ColaVLA moves reasoning from long textual chains into compact cognitive latents and generates hierarchical, causality-consistent trajectories in parallel. The design targets lower VLM latency while connecting high-level decisions to multi-scale continuous plans.

name: SpaceDrive
title: SpaceDrive: Infusing Spatial Awareness into VLM-based Autonomous Driving
summary: SpaceDrive represents 3D coordinates as positional encodings rather than textual number tokens, allowing VLMs to reason jointly about geometry and semantics. It derives spatial cues from multi-view depth, ego history, and language instructions and attaches them to visual tokens.

name: WAM-Flow
title: WAM-Flow: Parallel Coarse-to-Fine Motion Planning via Discrete Flow Matching for Autonomous Driving
summary: WAM-Flow turns trajectory planning into discrete flow matching, enabling parallel bidirectional denoising and coarse-to-fine refinement. A geometry-aware tokenizer and simulator-guided policy optimization balance safety, progress, and comfort with a tunable inference-cost trade-off.

name: OpenREAD
title: OpenREAD: Reinforced Open-Ended Reasoning for End-to-End Autonomous Driving with LLM-as-Critic
summary: OpenREAD trains an end-to-end driving VLM with open-ended reasoning reinforcement: an LLM critic scores reasoning quality, while a shared fine-tuning pipeline improves both scene reasoning and trajectory planning.

name: Alpamayo-R1
title: Alpamayo-R1: Bridging Reasoning and Action Prediction for Generalizable Autonomous Driving in the Long Tail
summary: Alpamayo-R1 combines causally grounded reasoning traces with a vision-language model and diffusion trajectory decoder, using supervised fine-tuning and reinforcement learning to align explanations with driving actions.

name: Cosmos-Predict2.5
title: World Simulation with Video Foundation Models for Physical AI
summary: Cosmos-Predict2.5 is a flow-based video world model for text-, image-, and video-conditioned generation, designed to support controllable synthetic data, policy evaluation, and closed-loop simulation for physical AI.

name: ReflectDrive-1
title: Discrete Diffusion for Reflective Vision-Language-Action Models in Autonomous Driving
summary: ReflectDrive discretizes driving trajectories and applies gradient-free reflection with local search and inpainting to iteratively replace unsafe actions with feasible alternatives.

name: OccVLA
title: OccVLA: Vision-Language-Action Model with Implicit 3D Occupancy Supervision
summary: OccVLA uses predicted 3D occupancy as implicit spatial reasoning and supervision for a vision-language-action model, improving driving planning without requiring occupancy inference at deployment.

name: FastDriveVLA
title: FastDriveVLA: Efficient End-to-End Driving via Plug-and-Play Reconstruction-based Token Pruning
summary: FastDriveVLA reduces visual-token cost with a plug-and-play reconstruction-based pruning method that preserves task-relevant image regions for efficient end-to-end driving.

name: AutoVLA
title: AutoVLA: A Vision-Language-Action Model for End-to-End Autonomous Driving with Adaptive Reasoning and Reinforcement Fine-Tuning
summary: AutoVLA unifies language reasoning and feasible trajectory tokens in one model, with fast and chain-of-thought modes and reinforcement fine-tuning to reduce needless reasoning.

name: ReCogDrive
title: ReCogDrive: A Reinforced Cognitive Framework for End-to-End Autonomous Driving
summary: ReCogDrive couples hierarchical driving-cognition data and a VLM with a diffusion planner, then applies reinforcement learning to improve trajectory safety and comfort.

name: DiffVLA
title: DiffVLA: Vision-Language Guided Diffusion Planning for Autonomous Driving
summary: DiffVLA combines VLM-guided decisions with a sparse-dense diffusion policy, using agent and map interactions to guide multimodal trajectory generation.

name: DriveMoE
title: DriveMoE: Mixture-of-Experts for Vision-Language-Action Model in End-to-End Autonomous Driving
summary: DriveMoE routes camera views and driving behaviors to specialized vision and action experts, aiming to handle varied maneuvers without averaging distinct actions.

name: LightEMMA
title: LightEMMA: A Longitudinal Evaluation of Vision-Language Models for Autonomous Driving
summary: LightEMMA evaluates successive VLMs under one lightweight, untuned driving protocol and finds that newer or larger models do not reliably improve prediction performance.

name: OpenDriveVLA
title: OpenDriveVLA: Towards End-to-end Autonomous Driving with Large Vision Language Action Model
summary: OpenDriveVLA aligns structured 2D/3D visual tokens with language and models agent-ego interactions to generate grounded trajectories and answer driving questions.

name: Cosmos-Reason1
title: Cosmos-Reason1: From Physical Common Sense To Embodied Reasoning
summary: Cosmos-Reason1 trains multimodal models for physical common sense and embodied decision-making, using structured reasoning data, supervised fine-tuning, and reinforcement learning.

name: AlphaDrive
title: AlphaDrive: Unleashing the Power of VLMs in Autonomous Driving via Reinforcement Learning and Reasoning
summary: AlphaDrive applies planning-specific reinforcement-learning rewards and a two-stage reasoning-and-planning training strategy to improve VLM driving decisions.

name: EMMA
title: EMMA: End-to-End Multimodal Model for Autonomous Driving
summary: EMMA maps camera inputs to trajectories, objects, and road graphs in a unified multimodal language space, with joint training improving performance across these tasks.

name: DriVLMe
title: DriVLMe: Enhancing LLM-Based Autonomous Driving Agents with Embodied and Social Experiences
summary: DriVLMe explores conversational, long-horizon driving with a video-language agent grounded in simulator experience and human dialogue, and documents its remaining real-world interaction and latency challenges.

name: DriveVLM
title: DriveVLM: The Convergence of Autonomous Driving and Large Vision-Language Models
summary: DriveVLM uses staged scene description, analysis, and hierarchical planning for complex scenarios; DriveVLM-Dual pairs it with a conventional driving stack and is tested on a production vehicle.

name: VLP
title: VLP: Vision Language Planning for Autonomous Driving
summary: VLP combines vision and language context for driving planning, targeting reasoning and long-tail generalization in urban scenes.

name: DriveLM
title: DriveLM: Driving with Graph Visual Question Answering
summary: DriveLM formulates driving perception, prediction, and planning as graph-structured visual question answering and releases data and an agent baseline.

name: DriveMLM
title: DriveMLM: Aligning Multi-Modal Large Language Models with Behavioral Planning States for Autonomous Driving
summary: DriveMLM connects multimodal language decisions to standard behavioral-planning states, enabling an LLM to make explainable closed-loop decisions within existing driving stacks.

name: LMDrive
title: LMDrive: Closed-Loop End-to-End Driving with Large Language Models
summary: LMDrive follows natural-language instructions in closed-loop driving by combining language with multimodal sensors, and introduces instruction-following data and the LangAuto benchmark.

name: Dolphins
title: Dolphins: Multimodal Language Model for Driving
summary: Dolphins instruction-tunes a multimodal language model for driving tasks, using grounded chain-of-thought to support scene understanding, instruction following, in-context adaptation, and reflection.

name: On the Road with GPT-4V
title: On the Road with GPT-4V(ision): Early Explorations of Visual-Language Model on Autonomous Driving
summary: On the Road with GPT-4V evaluates a multimodal model on driving-scene understanding, causal reasoning, and decisions, highlighting both its promise and gaps in spatial grounding and traffic-signal perception.

name: LanguageMPC
title: LanguageMPC: Large Language Models as Decision Makers for Autonomous Driving
summary: LanguageMPC uses LLM reasoning for complex driving decisions and translates them into commands for low-level controllers, targeting interpretability and generalization.

name: LLM-Driver
title: Driving with LLMs: Fusing Object-Level Vector Modality for Explainable Autonomous Driving
summary: Driving with LLMs aligns object-level vector inputs with a language model and introduces a 160K-pair driving QA dataset for explainable decisions and action generation.

name: GPT-Driver
title: GPT-Driver: Learning to Drive with GPT
summary: GPT-Driver casts motion planning as language generation, prompting and fine-tuning GPT to output coordinate-based trajectories with natural-language reasoning.

name: DriveGPT4
title: DriveGPT4: Interpretable End-to-End Autonomous Driving via Large Language Model
summary: DriveGPT4 fine-tunes a multimodal LLM on driving video and instruction data to explain vehicle behavior, answer questions, and predict low-level controls.

name: DiLu
title: DiLu: A Knowledge-Driven Approach to Autonomous Driving with Large Language Models
summary: DiLu equips an LLM driving agent with reasoning, reflection, and memory so it can accumulate experience and generalize decisions beyond fixed driving data.

name: Drive as You Speak
title: Drive as You Speak: Enabling Human-Like Interaction with Large Language Models in Autonomous Vehicles
summary: Drive as You Speak outlines an LLM-based vehicle framework that combines natural-language interaction, contextual reasoning, and specialized tools with existing driving modules.

name: DOROTHIE
title: DOROTHIE: Spoken Dialogue for Handling Unexpected Situations in Interactive Autonomous Driving Agents
summary: DOROTHIE introduces an interactive simulator and spoken-dialogue navigation benchmark for studying how driving agents handle unexpected events through human communication.

name: DreamStream
title: DreamStream: Towards Policy-Oriented Generative Simulation for End-to-End Driving
summary: DreamStream is a policy-oriented generative simulator that preserves decision-relevant scene structure for closed-loop driving evaluation and introduces the interactive Navhard-CL benchmark.

name: ZYT-World
title: ZYT-World: A Real-Time Controllable World Model for Closed-Loop Autonomous-Driving Simulation
summary: ZYT-World targets low-latency, controllable seven-camera driving simulation, combining camera-specific conditioning, one-step streaming generation, and place memory.

name: MM-Future
title: MM-Future: Multi-Mode Joint World-Action Modeling for Autonomous Driving
summary: MM-Future jointly generates multiple paired future-scene and ego-action hypotheses, then scores candidate trajectories using their predicted futures.

name: SV-WAM
title: SV-WAM: An Efficient Surround-View World-Action Model for End-to-End Autonomous Driving
summary: SV-WAM uses six-camera future-video prediction as training supervision for a shared world-action model, then removes the video branch for efficient planning.

name: VATIX
title: How Far Can 5,500 Hours of Driving Take You? A Scaling Law Analysis of Video Diffusion Models
summary: This study analyzes video-diffusion scaling on up to 5,500 hours of driving data and finds training exposure especially effective under fixed compute, while larger models improve asymptotic quality.

name: BehaviorWorldGen
title: BehaviorWorldGen: Closing the Loop between Action Models and World Simulators via Controllable Behavior-Aware Structured World Generation
summary: BehaviorWorldGen generates controllable multi-agent traffic rollouts whose agents respond to the ego and one another, then uses rendered scenarios to refine driving policies.

name: WA-JEPA
title: WA-JEPA: Rethinking the Video JEPA Paradigm for World-Action Modeling in Autonomous Driving
summary: WA-JEPA adapts video JEPA to action-conditioned driving futures with future-masked training, latent flow matching, and joint future-scene/trajectory prediction.

name: RISE
title: RISE: Adaptive Imagination for World Action Models
summary: RISE adaptively decides whether to continue world-model rollouts based on expected planning benefit and compute cost, supported by counterfactual risk data.

name: DA-WAM
title: DA-WAM: Decision-Aligned Future Latents for Driving World Models
summary: DA-WAM jointly trains action-conditioned future latents and trajectory scoring so each candidate is evaluated against its own predicted consequences.

name: 4D-WAM
title: 4D-WAM: 4D Consistent World Modeling for Autonomous Driving
summary: 4D-WAM uses geometric-model supervision to improve the physical consistency of predicted driving futures and emphasizes early denoising stages where planning decisions form.

name: SimWAM
title: SimWAM: A Simple World Action Model for End-to-End Autonomous Driving
summary: SimWAM uses future video as training-only supervision for a lightweight action expert, avoiding video generation at inference and adding reinforcement learning for driving rewards.

name: SUV
title: SUV: Future Scene Understanding as Video Generation for End-to-End Driving
summary: SUV predicts future visual, semantic, depth, and agent-dynamics streams with a shared video model, then conditions an action expert on those futures for trajectory planning.

name: Auto-JEPA
title: Auto-JEPA: A Latent World Model of Continuous Intent for End-to-End Autonomous Driving
summary: Auto-JEPA predicts a continuous future-driving-intent embedding and retrieves/ranks executable trajectories, avoiding dense future-scene reconstruction and a learned trajectory generator.

name: INTACT
title: INTACT: Isomorphic Intent-to-Action Learning for Search-Free World Models
summary: INTACT learns an intent-to-action interface from reward-free trajectories, enabling a direct policy from latent goals while retaining optional sampling or local search.

name: HyWorldVLA
title: HyWorldVLA: A Vision-Language-Action Model with Hybrid World Modeling for Autonomous Driving
summary: HyWorldVLA combines pixel-level video reconstruction with latent future prediction during training, then uses future latents to guide trajectory generation.

name: GeoWorldAD
title: GeoWorldAD: Geometry World Action Model for Autonomous Driving
summary: GeoWorldAD grounds planning in present 3D geometry and predicted future geometry, iteratively refining trajectories to balance safety and progress.

name: OWMDrive
title: OWMDrive: Causality-Aware End-to-End Autonomous Driving via 4D Occupancy World Model
summary: OWMDrive forecasts multi-step 3D occupancy as a causal future prior for diffusion-based trajectory planning in uncertain or partially observed scenes.

name: Metis
title: Metis: A Generalizable and Efficient World-Action Model for Autonomous Driving and Urban Navigation
summary: Metis separates video generation and action prediction into transformer experts that train jointly but let the planner skip video generation at inference.

name: NVIDIA OmniDreams
title: NVIDIA OmniDreams: Real-Time Generative World Model for Closed-Loop Autonomous Vehicle Simulation
summary: OmniDreams is an action-conditioned video world model for real-time closed-loop simulation, generating reactive observations for long-tail driving scenarios.

name: Cosmos 3
title: Cosmos 3: Omnimodal World Models for Physical AI
summary: Cosmos 3 is an omnimodal foundation world-model family that jointly processes and generates language, images, video, audio, and actions for physical AI.

name: X-Foresight
title: X-Foresight: A Joint Vision-Action Causal Forecasting Network via Predictive World Modeling
summary: X-Foresight integrates long-horizon, chunk-wise future-video prediction into a VLA so world dynamics and action control are trained together, with extra supervision for safety-critical moments.

name: Xiaomi EV World Model
title: Xiaomi Auto World Model: A Joint World Model Integrating Reconstruction and Generation for Autonomous Driving
summary: The Xiaomi Auto World Model combines sparse-query 3D Gaussian reconstruction with few-step causal video generation for consistent closed-loop simulation and data synthesis.

name: GEM
title: GEM: Gaussian Evolution Model for Occupancy Forecasting and Motion Planning
summary: GEM represents driving scenes as continuous dynamic 4D Gaussians, enabling non-autoregressive occupancy queries at arbitrary times and downstream motion planning.

name: EponaV2
title: EponaV2: Driving World Model with Comprehensive Future Reasoning
summary: EponaV2 predicts richer future geometry and semantic representations to strengthen scene reasoning for planning, then further tunes plans with flow-matching-based reinforcement learning.

name: HorizonDrive
title: HorizonDrive: Self-Corrective Autoregressive World Model for Long-horizon Driving Simulation
summary: HorizonDrive trains an autoregressive driving-video teacher to recover from rollout errors, extending reliable supervision to minute-scale simulation while keeping memory bounded.

name: DAWN
title: The DAWN of World-Action Interactive Models
summary: DAWN couples latent future-world prediction and action denoising in a short interactive rollout, iteratively refining the imagined scene and planned trajectory.

name: DeepSight
title: DeepSight: Long-Horizon World Modeling via Latent States Prediction for End-to-End Autonomous Driving
summary: DeepSight predicts parallel future BEV semantic latents for long-horizon world modeling and adds adaptive text reasoning to improve decisions in challenging scenarios.

name: CoWorld-VLA
title: CoWorld-VLA: Thinking in a Multi-Expert World Model for Autonomous Driving
summary: CoWorld-VLA supplies a planner with expert tokens for semantic interactions, geometry, dynamics, and ego goals, fusing them during diffusion-based trajectory generation.

name: DriveFuture
title: DriveFuture: Future-Aware Latent World Models for Autonomous Driving
summary: DriveFuture makes predicted future latent states an explicit condition for its diffusion trajectory planner, aligning future modeling with the decision being made.

name: X-Cache
title: X-Cache: Cross-Chunk Block Caching for Few-Step Autoregressive World Models Inference
summary: X-Cache accelerates few-step autoregressive world-model inference by selectively reusing transformer block computations across video chunks.

name: DriveVA
title: DriveVA: Video Action Models are Zero-Shot Drivers
summary: DriveVA jointly predicts videos and trajectories in a shared latent generative process, using video-model priors to support zero-shot transfer across driving domains.

name: ExploreVLA
title: ExploreVLA: Dense World Modeling and Exploration for End-to-End Autonomous Driving
summary: ExploreVLA uses future RGB and depth prediction both as dense world supervision and as an uncertainty-based novelty reward for safety-gated policy exploration.

name: DriveDreamer-Policy
title: DriveDreamer-Policy: A Geometry-Grounded World-Action Model for Unified Generation and Planning
summary: DriveDreamer-Policy unifies depth, future-video, and action generation, using explicit geometry to condition both world prediction and trajectory planning.

name: Uni-World VLA
title: Uni-World VLA: Interleaved World Modeling and Planning for Autonomous Driving
summary: Uni-World VLA interleaves future-frame prediction with trajectory generation so each planning step can react to the imagined scene, with monocular depth cues for geometry.

name: Latent-WAM
title: Latent-WAM: Latent World Action Modeling for End-to-End Autonomous Driving
summary: Latent-WAM compresses multi-view scenes into geometry-aware tokens and predicts causal future latents to guide efficient trajectory planning.

name: X-World
title: X-World: Controllable Ego-Centric Multi-Camera World Models for Scalable End-to-End Driving
summary: X-World is a controllable, action-conditioned multi-camera video world model designed for reproducible closed-loop policy evaluation with editable traffic and scene attributes.

name: Fast-WAM
title: Fast-WAM: Do World Action Models Need Test-time Future Imagination?
summary: Fast-WAM retains video co-training but skips future-video generation at inference, testing whether learned video representations alone can support faster world-action policies.

name: WorldDrive
title: Bridging Scene Generation and Planning: Driving with World Model via Unifying Vision and Motion Representation
summary: WorldDrive unifies trajectory-conditioned scene generation and motion representations, then uses a future-aware reward model to rank planning candidates.

name: ResWorld
title: ResWorld: Temporal Residual World Model for End-to-End Autonomous Driving
summary: ResWorld models temporal residuals to focus on dynamic actors, combines them with current static-scene features, and refines candidate paths using predicted future BEV.

name: DriveWorld-VLA
title: DriveWorld-VLA: Unified Latent-Space World Modeling with Vision-Language-Action for Autonomous Driving
summary: DriveWorld-VLA shares latent future-scene states directly with a language-action planner, enabling action-conditioned imagination without pixel-level rollout.

name: UniDWM
title: UniDWM: Towards a Unified Driving World Model via Multifaceted Representation Learning
summary: UniDWM learns structured, dynamic latent states with a shared reconstruction-and-generation design to support driving-scene understanding, future prediction, and planning.

name: Drive-JEPA
title: Drive-JEPA: Video JEPA Meets Multimodal Trajectory Distillation for End-to-End Driving
summary: Drive-JEPA adapts video JEPA to planning-relevant driving representations and distills diverse simulated and human trajectories into a multimodal planner.

name: UniDrive-WM
title: UniDrive-WM: Unified Understanding, Planning and Generation World Model for Autonomous Driving
summary: UniDrive-WM combines scene understanding, trajectory planning, and trajectory-conditioned future-image generation in one model, using generated futures as planning supervision.

name: DriveLaW
title: DriveLaW:Unifying Planning and Video Generation in a Latent Driving World
summary: DriveLaW feeds a video world model's latent features directly into a diffusion planner, aligning generated futures and planned motion through staged training.

name: WorldRFT
title: WorldRFT: Latent World Model Planning with Reinforcement Fine-Tuning for Autonomous Driving
summary: WorldRFT aligns latent scene representations with hierarchical planning and locally refined trajectories, then applies collision-aware reinforcement fine-tuning.

name: MindDrive
title: MindDrive: An All-in-One Framework Bridging World Models and Vision-Language Model for End-to-End Autonomous Driving
summary: MindDrive uses a world-action model for what-if scene simulation and candidate generation, then applies VLM-based safety, comfort, and efficiency evaluation.

name: SimScale
title: SimScale: Learning to Drive via Real-World Simulation at Scale
summary: SimScale synthesizes reactive, photorealistic driving scenarios and pseudo-expert trajectories from real logs, enabling policy gains that scale with generated data.

name: DriveVLA-W0
title: DriveVLA-W0: World Models Amplify Data Scaling Law in Autonomous Driving
summary: DriveVLA-W0 adds future-image prediction as dense self-supervision to VLA training and finds that world modeling strengthens performance scaling with more driving data.

name: WorldMirror
title: WorldMirror: Universal 3D World Reconstruction with Any-Prior Prompting
summary: WorldMirror is a general-purpose 3D reconstruction model that accepts varied geometric priors and predicts multiple scene representations in one feed-forward system.

name: RAP
title: RAP: 3D Rasterization Augmented End-to-End Planning
summary: RAP uses lightweight 3D rasterization to generate counterfactual views and recovery trajectories, then aligns raster features with real data for robust planner training.

name: IRL-VLA
title: IRL-VLA: Training an Vision-Language-Action Policy via Reward World Model
summary: IRL-VLA trains a driving policy with a lightweight inverse-reinforcement-learning reward world model, enabling closed-loop policy optimization without relying on expensive high-fidelity simulation.

name: World4Drive
title: World4Drive: End-to-End Autonomous Driving via Intention-aware Physical Latent World Model
summary: World4Drive learns intention-aware latent futures and uses a world-model selector to compare multimodal trajectories without requiring perception annotations.

name: EponaV1
title: Epona: Autoregressive Diffusion World Model for Autonomous Driving
summary: Epona models driving video with autoregressive diffusion and separates temporal dynamics from detailed frame generation, while integrating trajectory planning.

name: WoTE
title: End-to-End Driving with Online Trajectory Evaluation via BEV World Model
summary: WoTE uses a BEV world model to forecast trajectory outcomes and evaluate candidate paths efficiently in open- and closed-loop benchmarks.

name: Cosmos-Transfer1
title: Cosmos-Transfer1: Conditional World Generation with Adaptive Multimodal Control
summary: Cosmos-Transfer enables controllable world-to-world generation from spatial inputs such as segmentation, depth, and edges, including autonomous-driving data enrichment.

name: HERMES
title: HERMES: A Unified Self-Driving World Model for Simultaneous 3D Scene Understanding and Generation
summary: HERMES unifies BEV-based 3D scene understanding and future-scene generation, injecting contextual world knowledge through causal world queries.

name: Cosmos
title: Cosmos World Foundation Model Platform for Physical AI
summary: Cosmos is a foundation-model platform for building customized physical-AI world models, with video curation tools, pretrained models, and tokenizers.

name: GaussianAD
title: GaussianAD: Gaussian-Centric End-to-End Autonomous Driving
summary: GaussianAD represents driving scenes with dynamic 3D semantic Gaussians to support perception, occupancy forecasting, and end-to-end motion planning.

name: LAW
title: Enhancing End-to-End Autonomous Driving with Latent World Model
summary: LAW predicts future latent scene features from current observations and ego trajectories, adding self-supervised supervision to improve end-to-end planning.

name: Vista
title: Vista: A Generalizable Driving World Model with High Fidelity and Versatile Controllability
summary: Vista is a controllable driving world model designed for high-fidelity, long-horizon predictions that generalize across environments and action conditions.

name: GenAD
title: Generalized Predictive Model for Autonomous Driving
summary: GenAD is a large-scale latent-diffusion driving-video predictor trained on diverse web videos, with adaptations for action-conditioned prediction and motion planning.

name: WoVoGen
title: WoVoGen: World Volume-aware Diffusion for Controllable Multi-camera Driving Scene Generation
summary: WoVoGen predicts a controllable 4D world volume and uses it to generate spatially and temporally consistent multi-camera driving videos.

name: Drive-WM
title: Driving into the Future: Multiview Visual Forecasting and Planning with World Model for Autonomous Driving
summary: Drive-WM generates controllable multi-view futures for candidate maneuvers and uses image-based rewards to select a safer driving trajectory.

name: OccWorld
title: OccWorld: Learning a 3D Occupancy World Model for Autonomous Driving
summary: OccWorld tokenizes 3D occupancy and autoregressively predicts both future scenes and ego trajectories, without relying on instance or map labels.

name: ADriver-I
title: ADriver-I: A General World Model for Autonomous Driving
summary: ADriver-I interleaves vision and action tokens to iteratively predict controls and future frames, enabling the policy to act within its own generated world.

name: DrivingDiffusion
title: DrivingDiffusion: Layout-Guided multi-view driving scene video generation with latent diffusion model
summary: DrivingDiffusion generates multi-camera driving videos from 3D layouts, combining cross-view communication, temporal modeling, and long-video processing.

name: GAIA-1
title: GAIA-1: A Generative World Model for Autonomous Driving
summary: GAIA-1 is a video-, text-, and action-conditioned generative driving world model that predicts discrete sequences to produce controllable future scenarios.

name: DriveDreamer
title: DriveDreamer: Towards Real-world-driven World Models for Autonomous Driving
summary: DriveDreamer learns traffic structure and future-state generation from real-world driving data, producing controllable videos and policy-relevant scenarios.

name: MILE
title: Model-Based Imitation Learning for Urban Driving
summary: MILE jointly learns a compact latent world model and driving policy from offline videos, enabling planning through imagined future states.

name: World on Rails
title: Learning to Drive from a World on Rails
summary: World on Rails learns a vision-based driving policy from logged data using a non-reactive world model to evaluate and supervise candidate trajectories.

name: DriveGAN
title: DriveGAN: Towards a Controllable High-Quality Neural Simulation
summary: DriveGAN learns a controllable, differentiable neural driving simulator directly from video and action pairs, allowing actions and scene attributes such as weather to be varied.

name: OPTED
title: OPTED: On-Policy Fine-Tuning for End-to-End Driving using a Render-Free Teacher
summary: OPTED fine-tunes a pretrained driving policy in closed loop using a privileged RL teacher, reducing the simulator interactions needed for post-training.

name: Self-Improving Autonomous Vehicles
title: Self-Improving Autonomous Vehicles via Real-World Reinforcement Learning
summary: This real-world reinforcement-learning method selects informative driving situations and aborts episodes before unsafe states, allowing vehicles to improve with less human intervention.

name: CL4AD
title: Scaling Curriculum Learning For Autonomous Driving
summary: CL4AD applies curriculum learning to large-scale driving simulators, prioritizing scenarios by learning utility to improve sample efficiency over uniform randomization.

name: AlignADV
title: From Attacks to Curricula: Learnability-Guided Adversarial Training for Safe Autonomous Driving
summary: AlignADV generates adversarial yet learnable driving scenarios and samples them according to the evolving policy's capabilities, improving training efficiency and safety.

name: EvoDrive
title: EvoDrive: Pareto Evolution for Safety-Critical Autonomous Driving via Self-Improving LLM Agents
summary: EvoDrive evolves traffic-scenario generators and evaluators through simulator-grounded LLM agents, preserving a Pareto set of diverse realism-versus-adversariality trade-offs.

name: Agentic AI + SkillBank
title: Agentic AI in Autonomous Driving: LLM-Enhanced RL with Reusable Skills and Adaptive Exploration for Enhanced Safety
summary: This framework combines PPO with an LLM-guided SkillBank of reusable maneuvers and curiosity-driven exploration to improve driving safety and learning stability.

name: Dense Learning
title: Breaking through safety performance stagnation in autonomous vehicles with dense learning
summary: Dense learning selects informative failures and successes, including near misses, to reduce variance in safety-critical policy training while preserving unbiased learning.

name: Safe-Evolving RL
title: An Uncertainty-Aware Safe-Evolving Reinforcement Learning Algorithm for Decision-Making and Control in Highway Autonomous Driving
summary: This highway-driving method combines internal and external stability with safety mechanisms, using uncertainty awareness to support safer reinforcement-learning evolution.

name: Mechanism-Experience Learning
title: A Safe and Efficient Self-Evolving Algorithm for Decision-Making and Control of Autonomous Driving Systems
summary: Mechanism-Experience Learning narrows the RL search space with human-like driving tendencies and constrains exploration with a safety-aware mechanistic model.

name: Expert-Agent Feedback
title: Integrating Expert-Agent Bi-Directional Positive Feedback for Autonomous Driving Through Reinforcement Learning
summary: This expert-guided RL framework lets an agent surpass an imperfect expert while using high-quality agent experience to improve the expert policy in return.

name: Safe Self-Evolution with Risk Quantification
title: A Safe Self-Evolution Algorithm for Autonomous Driving Based on Data-Driven Risk Quantification Model
summary: A data-driven risk model estimates the safety of candidate driving actions and guides policy updates, allowing the controller to improve its performance while explicitly accounting for risk.

name: Gigaflow
title: Robust Autonomy Emerges from Self-Play
summary: Gigaflow enables large-scale simulator self-play, showing that robust, naturalistic driving policies can emerge without human driving demonstrations.

name: Human Feedback for Intelligent Driving
title: Human Feedback Enhanced Autonomous Intelligent Systems: A Perspective from Intelligent Driving
summary: This perspective proposes a self-evolving intelligent-driving framework that uses human demonstrations, evaluations, interventions, and prior knowledge to guide policy learning.

name: DCARL
title: Continuous Improvement of Self-Driving Cars Using Dynamic Confidence-Aware Reinforcement Learning
summary: DCARL uses confidence-aware reinforcement learning to improve driving policies from collected experience while reverting to a safer baseline in uncertain situations.

name: Self-Improving Safety RL
title: Self-Improving Safety Performance of Reinforcement Learning Based Driving with Black-Box Verification Algorithms
summary: This framework uses black-box verification to discover RL driving failures, then retrains the policy on those scenarios to improve safety.

name: Trustworthy Improvement RL
title: Trustworthy Safety Improvement for Autonomous Driving Using Reinforcement Learning
summary: This method improves a rule-based driving controller with reinforcement learning and uses a value-based safety gate to deploy the learned policy only when it is expected to outperform the trusted baseline.
